dedupe_keys.name: an open data infrastructure for the study of anthropogenic hazards linked to georesource exploitation

description: An open data infrastructure for the study of anthropogenic hazards linked to georesource exploitation is a data set described in a peer-reviewed Scientific Data article written by Beata Orlecka-Sikora et al. Mining, water-reservoir impoundment, underground gas storage, geothermal energy exploitation and hydrocarbon extraction have the potential to cause rock deformation and earthquakes, which may be hazardous for people, infrastructure and the environment. Restricted access to data constitutes a barrier to assessing and mitigating the associated hazards. Coverage: a single site or case study; published in 2020. The formats are not stated in the sources read. The paper's page was read, but no repository address could be taken from its machine-readable metadata, so the record links to the article, whose Data Records section names where the data sit. Access is free of charge and open according to the article. The licence is CC-BY-4.0, taken from the Data Records or Data Availability section of the paper. Caveats: written from the Scientific Data article metadata (title, abstract, Data Records section) read on 2026-10-01; the data themselves were not opened or downloaded, so their contents, quality and current availability were not checked. It can support multi-sector infrastructure risk and planning studies. Related records: none catalogued yet.
